title: UI/使用性テストと操作効率検証

frozenPlan.note: The original criteria remain preserved. User subsequently rejected the absolute vertical travel observed by the test; the historical plan is not rewritten after execution.

humanUsabilityDecision.reason: Absolute vertical travel is unacceptable even though direction-reversal counts were within the original frozen budget.

firstDelete.note: After deleting the 196-item workload, both GitHub and the visible project list converged from 2 to 1 and only the C-04 plan remained.

visibleStaleProjects: C-04 UI負荷・使用性テスト 196項目（取込）
C-04 UI/使用性テスト計画 v1（取込）

rootCause.summary: An older in-flight loadRecords result can overwrite newer state after delete/reload because loadRecords applies state.records without a latest-generation guard and deleteProject does not invalidate older record loads.
proof: The first delete converged to one visible project.
The final delete reduced GitHub Contents API project count to zero.
After the zero-state reload, both previously deleted project cards reappeared visibly, which can only be reconstructed from an earlier two-row load result.
The current loadRecords implementation always assigns state.records=rows and has no request generation, cancellation, or latest-wins check.

goals: Reduce absolute mobile/desktop vertical travel, not merely scroll-direction reversals.
Make primary project actions and tabs reachable without returning through tens of thousands of pixels.
Make any one of 196 items directly reachable without traversing all preceding cards.
candidateChanges: Replace the full mobile sidebar stack with a compact workspace header plus project/action drawer.
Keep project actions and the Overview/Items/AI handoff/Advanced JSON tabs sticky within the usable viewport.
Add item search by ID/title plus kind/status filters.
Replace 196 continuously expanded cards with compact rows and progressive disclosure, backed by pagination or virtualization.
Provide direct jump to an item and grouped status/issue shortcuts.
Keep Core sync and Stage B guide collapsed so they do not occupy primary interaction space.
proposedNextAcceptance: A primary task must not require traversal through the complete item corpus.
Any item must be reachable using search/filter/jump without scrolling through prior items.
Primary actions and tabs remain accessible within at most one viewport of return travel.
Absolute vertical travel will be measured and capped in the C-04 v2 plan before retest.

blocker: Do not start D-01 until C-04 user-visible delete/reload and revised vertical-traversal acceptance pass.
